name: Sculpfun C2 14W
tagline: A 1.6 kg open-frame diode with a 300 × 300 mm bed that cuts 8 mm basswood, for $239
tldr: The C2 14W is the stronger version of Sculpfun's new compact engraver, listed on Sculpfun's store in October 2026 at $239. It weighs 1.6 kg, works on a 300 × 300 mm area and moves at up to 20,000 mm/min. Sculpfun gives a 0.06 × 0.06 mm spot and single-pass cuts in 8 mm basswood and 5 mm black acrylic. Focus is set with a built-in lever, and the frame has X and Y limit switches. It is an open frame without an enclosure or air pump in the box, and no independent test exists yet.
mainObjective: Engraving and light cutting of wood and dark acrylic on a small desk, at a starter budget

priceRange.note: Official Sculpfun store, Nov 2026: $239 for the C2 14W, same price with US, EU, UK or AU plug; the C2 7W is $179

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

cut: Basswood up to 8 mm in one pass (Sculpfun rating)
Black acrylic up to 5 mm in one pass (Sculpfun rating)

pros: Single-pass cuts in 8 mm basswood and 5 mm black acrylic according to Sculpfun, for $239
300 × 300 mm area in a 1.6 kg frame that stores easily, four times the area of the earlier Sculpfun C1
Lever focus and X/Y limit switches: quick to set up and to home
cons: Open frame: no enclosure, so safety glasses and smoke extraction are up to you
Air assist, honeycomb panel and rotary roller are all optional extras
Very new machine: cutting figures are Sculpfun's own, with no independent test yet
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 14W version of the Sculpfun C2. Take it over the 7W if you plan to cut wood or dark acrylic: Sculpfun rates it for 8 mm basswood against 5 mm, for $60 more. The frame, area and software are the same on both versions. Sculpfun Space, the free software, runs on Windows; the Mac version is announced but not out yet, so Mac users should plan on LightBurn.
proTips: Add the optional air assist before cutting: it clears smoke from the cut and reduces scorching. Put a honeycomb panel or a sacrificial board under the work, as the frame has no bed. Run a test grid on each new plywood batch, since glue layers vary.

editorialDepth.advantages: The C2 14W puts real cutting ability in a frame that weighs 1.6 kg and costs $239. The 300 × 300 mm area covers coasters, ornaments, signs and small boxes, and the lever focus and limit switches remove two common beginner mistakes: a wrong focus height and a head that hits the frame.
editorialDepth.limitations: It is an open frame with no enclosure, no air pump and no bed in the box, so the real cost rises once you add air assist and a honeycomb panel. The cutting thicknesses are Sculpfun's ratings, without stated speeds, and the machine is too new for independent tests.

faq.question: How thick can the Sculpfun C2 14W cut?
faq.answer: Sculpfun rates the 14W module for 8 mm basswood and 5 mm black acrylic in a single pass. It does not publish the speed used, and no independent test confirms these figures yet. Plywood, which has glue layers, cuts slower than basswood.

faq.question: C2 14W or C2 7W?
faq.answer: The 14W costs $239 against $179 for the 7W (Sculpfun store, November 2026). The 14W is rated for 8 mm basswood and 5 mm black acrylic, the 7W for 5 mm and 3 mm. The 7W has a finer spot, 0.04 mm against 0.06 mm, so it suits buyers who only engrave.

faq.question: Can the C2 14W engrave metal?
faq.answer: It marks anodized aluminum and coated metal, and Sculpfun lists 304 stainless steel among the engraving materials. For regular marking on bare metal, Sculpfun sells a 1.2W infrared module for the C2 separately.
